name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> with domain 'play' (sibling fns fd2_play_ending_and_record_clear / fd2_play_game_ending_cinematic share it). Descriptor 'chapter_clear_fanfare' accurately reflects the 2-frame chapter-cleared fanfare it plays. No Ghidra address residue in the name.
purpose: Plays the short 2-frame 'chapter cleared' fanfare sprite sequence after a chapter is beaten.
logic_summary: Stops BGM with fade; waits 1 BIOS tick; fades screen to black; loads FDOTHER.DAT[0x4F] fanfare sprite sheet; clears the 64000-byte VGA framebuffer at 0xA0000; blits frame 0 at pitch 0x140 with transparent color -1; fades the palette in to reveal frame 0; holds 9 ticks; blits frame 1; holds 0x24 (36) ticks; frees the sprite sheet. void/void; tail free() compiles into the shared free-wrapper epilogue (PUSH EBX; JMP 0x15E94).

returns.semantics: No return value; pure side-effect (audio/video) routine.

comment_original_issue: Src header said the caller enters 'when game_event_flag == 1' using a generic placeholder name; the live global is data_fd2_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code (main checks == 1 = chapter cleared). Otherwise the block was accurate and concise.
notes: Confirmed via main @ 0x25BF4 decompile: call site reached only when data_fd2_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code == 1; main clears that code to 0 after return. Disassembly confirms 0x51a4d == FDOTHER.DAT string, EBX holds the sprite ptr across both blits, and the tail is PUSH EBX; JMP 0x15E94 (free-wrapper epilogue). __CHK(0x1c) is the standard Watcom stack-check prologue; decompiler in_stack_* locals are CHK artifacts, not real params. Src comment edited (single block) to use the live global name; Ghidra plate updated to match (kept full body breakdown, added the free tail-jump note).
